title: Customer status rollforward advisory — duplicated-response incident and remediations
content:
Executive summary:

On 2029-06-01 we observed intermittent duplicated responses for a subset of tenant requests routed through the US-West region. The behavior resulted in customers receiving two conversational completions where one was expected. No customer data exfiltration or cross-tenant leakage has been identified. Impact was limited to response duplication (confusing outputs and additional token usage).

This doc is a customer-facing rollforward advisory: it explains what happened in plain language, what we did to stop the problem, what we are doing to permanently fix it, and how customers can validate their integrations. We will publish an abbreviated status page entry and follow with a formal postmortem targeted to customers once internal RCA completes.

Scope and affected audiences:

- Affected subset: ~2.7% of requests routed through US-West between 2029-06-01 03:12 UTC and 2029-06-01 05:47 UTC.
- Customer impact: duplicated completions returned for some streaming and non-streaming text generation calls. Customers may have seen repeated sentences or a fully repeated response block.
- Likely affected product surfaces: Redwood API (text generation / chat) when using model routing policies that included regional fallbacks. Dedicated/Private deployments not managed by Redwood control plane are unaffected unless configured to use Redwood routing across regions.

Immediate actions (what we did within the incident window):

1) Automated mitigation: At 03:40 UTC we detected an unusual spike in duplicate-response signatures in telemetry and triggered the automated routing circuit-breaker for US-West fallthrough routing to start rejecting fallthrough routes that could trigger duplicate in-flight delivery. This reduced duplicates by ~85% within the next 6 minutes.
2) Manual containment: Routing engineers reverted a recent canary change to cross-region fallback batching that had been deployed earlier that morning; the revert completed at 04:12 UTC.
3) Cache hygiene: We identified a race between the regional prefix-KV cache invalidation and the routing service's async fan-out. We issued a targeted KV eviction for the affected worker pool at 04:45 UTC. Post eviction, duplication metrics dropped to baseline by 05:10 UTC.
4) Customer communication: A succinct status page entry was posted at 05:20 UTC to notify affected customers of ongoing mitigation.

Root hypothesis (interim):

Preliminary analysis indicates the duplication was caused by a timing window in which the routing service attempted a fallthrough path while the regional KV prefix cache still contained stale in-flight markers. When the routing service retried through an alternative replica concurrently with the original in-flight worker (which had not yet recorded completion), both workers completed and both completions were surfaced to the caller. The recently deployed change to batching and async fan-out widened the timing window and increased the probability of that race.

Why this matters to customers:

- UX confusion: Some conversational sessions may contain duplicated sentences or blocks, which can be interpreted as model hallucination or unexpected behavior.
- Unit economics: For a small fraction of requests, customers may have consumed double the expected token budget for a single logical response. We understand cost sensitivity and are reviewing credit/adjustment policy options for affected tenants.

What we are doing next (short-term and medium-term):

Short-term (within 48 hours):
- Full rollback of the cross-region batching change in all regions where it was recently rolled out.
- Add a server-side de-duplication filter for a broad class of duplication signatures (non-invasive and opt-out disabled by default) — will be enabled as emergency protection while a deeper fix is implemented.
- Issue a limited customer credit for measured duplicated token charges for tenants identified in the event window (customer-success will reach out to impacted accounts).

Medium-term (2–4 weeks):
- Fix the race by making in-flight completion markers strongly consistent for the routing RPC pattern, removing the timing dependency between KV invalidation and async fan-out.
- Harden pre-deploy chaos tests to simulate concurrent fallthrough retries + KV staleness to prevent recurrence.
- Improve telemetry to show causal traces when a request results in >1 completion, including request-id correlation across services.

Longer-term (quarterly):
- Rework model routing fallback primitives to be idempotent by design (idempotency keys surfaced to customer SDKs and persisted at the routing layer).
- Add explicit per-request cost-attribution logs so customers can reconcile token counts per logical response.

Customer actions and validation checklist (what customers can do now):

- Check recent sessions: If you noticed duplicated sentences between 2029-06-01 03:12 UTC and 05:47 UTC, please open a ticket with the request-ids or session timestamps. We will attach token usage and traces to help you reconcile billing and UX impact.
- Defensive SDK change (optional): If your integration uses streaming outputs and you have client-side dedup logic, consider enabling tolerant deduplication for the next 48 hours. We will publish guidance in the support article.
- Feature flags: If you rely on private deployments with cross-region fallbacks, consider temporarily disabling cross-region fallthrough until we confirm the hardened rollout (>2 weeks). Contact your solutions engineer for a safe config.

Billing and credits:

We will proactively calculate duplicated-token exposure for tenants identified in the impacted cohort. Customer-success will contact account owners with proposed credits and a reconciliation report. If you prefer an immediate investigation of a specific session, please include request-id and approximate timestamp; we will prioritize.

What we will publish to the status page (short form):

Title: Intermittent duplicated responses (US-West) — mitigated
Summary: Between 03:12–05:47 UTC on 2029-06-01 a small percentage of requests routed via US-West returned duplicated completions. The issue has been mitigated and a rollback and KV eviction prevented further duplication. Customers with affected sessions will be contacted.
Impact: Response duplication, potential additional token usage; no data leakage.
Next update: Formal customer postmortem (next 7 business days).

Q&A (anticipated customer questions):

Q: Did any customer data get exposed to another customer?
A: No. We have found no evidence of cross-tenant data leakage. The duplication resulted in two completions of the same request, not cross-tenant mixing.

Q: Will you refund the extra tokens charged?
A: We will propose a targeted credit for affected tenants; customer-success will reach out with reconciliation details. Customers who open a ticket with request-ids will receive expedited review.

Q: How will you prevent this from recurring?
A: We will deliver a multi-stage fix: rollback, emergency de-dup filter, strong consistency for in-flight markers, improved chaos tests, and idempotency primitives for routing.

Contacts and escalation path:

- Primary contact: Aisha Kapoor (customer-success lead) — aisha.kapoor@redwood.ai
- Technical liaison: Michael Chen (routing eng) — michael.chen@redwood.ai
- Dedicated customers: your named solutions engineer or account team will reach out directly.

Appendix (technical notes for engineers / SEs):

- Observability: Look for duplication signature metric: routing.duplicate_completions.count with tag region=us-west and model=<model-name>.
- Short traces: request-id + router-trace-id in logs correlate both completions back to the same client request.
- Temporary mitigations already in place: cross-region batching rollback + targeted KV eviction + automated circuit-breaker on fallthrough routes.

We will update this document and the public status page as the RCA completes. Customer-success will coordinate credits and account-level follow-ups starting 2029-06-04.

Document history:
- 2029-06-01 06:20 UTC — initial draft (Aisha Kapoor)

- 2029-06-03 09:12 UTC — in_review with CS and routing eng (Priya Natarajan)

End of advisory.
